patch.reason: ADR 0031, GitHub #268: the hq-e8-2b verify route of the small-T kernel measured 6.2 us per GQA layer per 1K keys per lane against a 0.96 us MMA floor (docs/findings/2026-09-24-hq-attention-at-long-context.md), and Nsight Compute at 8 lanes x 30K put 80% of its instructions in the tile decode at 35% issue, latency-bound at 8 warps per SM with the q fragments and accumulators holding 192 of 255 registers. The throughput form (IgnisThroughput, default) at <= 48 query rows (27B at width 8; wider geometries run the reference form): q kept in shared memory while K and V take turns in one tile, each role's code rows staged one phase ahead by cp.async, hq_decode_row_group_fast called by every warp at once, paired fragment loads; IgnisThroughput = false is the reference hq route, unchanged. Bit-exact against it: ignis_kernel_hq_verify_exact_test (11 shapes: widths 1-8, masks, offsets, permuted table rows, residual window with cleared ring slots, the fused append, split capacities 4/23/40/85; every partial and cache byte). Kernel alone: 8 lanes x 30K 1679 -> 890 us, 1 lane x 59K 368 -> 201 us. docs/findings/2026-09-24-hq-verify-decode-cost.md.

ADR 0037 correctness patch (GitHub #258, spec runtime/07): with the hq-e8-2b residual window on, the reference appends a prefill chunk before it attends, and the append rewrites the ring slots (key & 511) of the 512 keys before the chunk with the chunk's own rows, so a query is served keys up to ~1,000 positions after it. The hq route with the window on attends first and appends after (it never reads the chunk's codes: the fresh pass stages them); every other route keeps the reference's order. Fails without it: ignis_kernel_hq_route_agreement_test, the prefill-after-history arms (exact-window agreement with BF16 and bit-exact causality, dense, masked and banded).

ADR 0031: upstream ee9d5192 (PR #204), hand-merged onto the fork's Windows TMA descriptor and mbarrier spellings. The W4A4 TMA CTAs are rasterised token-fastest so the CTAs sharing a weight tile run together, and each activation-scale box is fetched once per pair of K tiles into a two-slot buffer; stage counts are limited to 2 or 3, where the slot reuse is safe (upstream allows >= 2). Output bit-identical. Upstream: operator x1.09-1.20, prefill +7.7..9.3%. ignis A/B: docs/findings/2026-09-24-upstream-quick-wins-ab.md.

Spec image-model/03 (ignis GitHub #320): a registry extension sanctioned for the image model's W8 vision tower (Qwen3-VL-8B), not an ADR 0031 bottleneck nor an ADR 0037 bug. select_w8_a16_launch registers the tower's qkv [3456,1152], output [1152,1152] and fc1 [4304,1152], the patch embedding [1152,1536], fc2 [1152,4304] (stored K 4352, the padded path) and the merger's and DeepStack mergers' fc2 [4096,4608], all on SIMT to T=16, then mma_r64_c128. The three K-1152 arms ran on SIMT at every T until ignis #324: the MMA kernel copies eight groups' scales as one 16-byte cp.async, which misaligns at K 1152 (72 bytes a row: wrong outputs at T=17, a misaligned-address fault at T=4096); src/ops/linear/w8/w8_rowsplit_gemm_mma.cuh's ADR 0031 patch now stages such a row in 8-byte halves. Every existing arm is unchanged. linear_workspace_capacity_bytes (kernel/src/linear.cu) asks select_w8_launch, so it admits the same problems. Test: ignis_kernel_w8_linear_tests, the six new shapes (T 1 to 49200), which throw 'w8 linear: unsupported shape or T' without it.

ADR 0031, a measured bottleneck (ignis GitHub #324, spec image-model/03). stage_w copies a window of eight groups' scales as one 16-byte cp.async, which needs a row of scales (padded K / 16 bytes) to be a multiple of 16 bytes. When it is a multiple of 8 but not of 16 (padded K an odd multiple of 128: the image model's vision tower at K 1152, 72 bytes), the patch copies the window as two 8-byte cp.async halves and zero-fills a half past the row. Every other row takes the unchanged 16-byte copy, so the problems routed here before compute bit for bit what they did (FNV-1a of the output at 322 problem/T pairs, before and after). The measurement: in an nsys capture of the ten-image edit encode (image_encoder_edit_gpu), w8_rowsplit_gemm_simt_kernel, which ran the tower's K-1152 linears (qkv [3456,1152], output [1152,1152], fc1 [4304,1152]), was 73% of all kernel time (9.99 of 13.63 s), at 9-13 TFLOPS against a bf16 bound near 210. On mma_r64_c128 they run at 150-183 TFLOPS, and the ten-image tower goes from 2.68 s to 0.43 s. Test: ignis_kernel_w8_linear_tests, the K-1152 cases from T 17: with the dispatch's MMA arms and without this patch, [3456,1152] gives wrong outputs at T=17 and T=64 and a misaligned-address fault at T=128.
